question: A 45-year-old male with a BMI of 34 kg/m² presents to the clinic for a routine check-up. Which of the following conditions is most directly associated with obesity and significantly increases perioperative risk due to airway management challenges?

A 2-year-old boy is diagnosed with a unilateral undescended testis located in the inguinal canal. While malignancy is a feared long-term risk, which of the following is the most common associated surgical finding/complication at the time of presentation or repair?

A patient presents with recurrent perianal discharge and pain. On examination, an external opening is noted. Which of the following is considered the gold standard "first-line" imaging modality for accurately mapping the anatomy of a complex fistula-in-ano before surgery?
During a screening colonoscopy, several polyps are identified and removed. Which of the following histological types carries the highest risk of progressing to adenocarcinoma?

A 25-year-old male presents with acute scrotal pain and swelling diagnosed as epididymo-orchitis. Which of the following organisms is least likely to be the primary causative agent in a sexually active young male?

A 30-year-old patient requires a kidney transplant. His brother is found to be a compatible match and agrees to donate. What is this transfer of tissue between two genetically non-identical members of the same species is defined as?

A 70-year-old male presents with right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain and a WBC count of 15,000/mm3. He is afebrile and has no other significant medical comorbidities. An ultrasound confirms acute cholecystitis. What is the most appropriate definitive management?
A lean man living in a tropical region presents with a history of recurrent high-grade fever, chills, and massive splenomegaly. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Hirschsprung disease is characterized by the absence of ganglion cells in the myenteric and submucosal plexuses. Which anatomical region is always involved in this condition?

A patient undergoes a laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. In addition to weight loss, the patient experiences a significant improvement in type 2 diabetes mellitus. Which hormonal change is primarily responsible for the early reduction in appetite?

A patient with a BMI of 38 kg/m2 and poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus is seeking bariatric surgery. Which procedure is often favored for its superior metabolic effects on glycemic control compared to restrictive procedures alone?
A 60-year-old male is diagnosed with a superficial (T1), low-grade transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder. What is the initial gold standard treatment?

During a physical examination of a patient with an inguinal hernia, the clinician performs the internal ring occlusion test. If the hernia still protrudes despite firm occlusion of the internal ring, what is the diagnosis?

A woman presents with a 3.5 cm epigastric swelling that has a positive cough impulse. She is symptomatic with occasional pain. What is the most appropriate surgical management for an adult with a defect of this size?
In clinical practice, the size of catheters and surgical tubes is often expressed in the French (Fr) scale. One French unit is mathematically equivalent to which of the following?

answers.option: Circumference of the tube in cm
Radius of the tube in mm
Circumference of the tube in mm
Diameter of the tube multiplied by 3

question: A hematologist refers a patient for an elective splenectomy. Which of the following is considered the most common indication for elective splenectomy in clinical practice?

A clinician palpates a smooth, firm mass in the right hypochondrium of an asymptomatic woman. Imaging identifies it as a Riedel lobe. Which of the following statements regarding this finding is incorrect?

answers.option: It is frequently palpable in the mid-axillary or mid-clavicular line
It is more commonly found in females
It is a developmental extension of the right lobe of the liver
It is a normal anatomical variant of the liver
It is a developmental extension of the left lobe of the liver

question: Embryological failure of the vitellointestinal duct to obliterate can result in various anomalies. What is the most common clinical remnant of this structure?

answers.option: Fibrous band connecting ileum to umbilicus

question: A 50-year-old patient presents with a long-standing umbilical hernia. Previously reducible, it is now larger, painful, and cannot be reduced. The patient is passing flatus and feces, has no vomiting, and no systemic signs of toxicity. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient with suspected carcinoid syndrome has an ultrasound showing hypoechoic lesions in the liver and an elevated 24-hour urinary 5-HIAA. What is the most appropriate next step to localize the primary tumor, typically found in the midgut?

A man is hit in the epigastrium by a bull. An X-ray shows a "sentinel loop" (focal ileus) in the upper abdomen, and an ultrasound reveals free fluid in the lesser sac. Which retroperitoneal structure is most likely injured by this blunt impact?

A 45-year-old patient is diagnosed with a 3 cm Esophageal Leiomyoma located in the muscularis propria of the mid-esophagus. The mucosa is intact. What is the surgical treatment of choice for this benign lesion?

A 60-year-old patient is incidentally found to have a 2 cm cystic lesion in the head of the pancreas. Imaging shows a characteristic "central stellate scar" with calcification. CEA and amylase levels from the cyst fluid are low. What is the most likely diagnosis?

The spleen plays a critical role in protecting the body against Overwhelming Post-Splenectomy Infection (OPSI), particularly from encapsulated bacteria. Which function is primarily responsible for this protection?

A patient undergoes a laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. In addition to weight loss, the patient experiences a significant improvement in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. Which hormonal change is primarily responsible for the early reduction in appetite?

A patient who recently suffered from acute pancreatitis now presents with a localized fluid collection. Which of the following is the most important biochemical marker to check in the aspirated fluid to differentiate a pseudocyst from other collections?

A patient who underwent an excisional hemorrhoidectomy earlier today presents with acute, massive rectal bleeding that has soaked his clothes and bedsheets. He is tachycardic and hypotensive. As the resident on call, what is the immediate definitive step to control the hemorrhage?

answers.option: Proctoscopy with anal packing at the bedside
Take to the operating theatre for exploration under anesthesia and hemostasis

question: A 65-year-old woman presents with involuntary leakage of urine during coughing and sneezing. While a clinical history and physical exam are vital, which of the following investigations is considered the gold standard for classifying the type of incontinence and guiding surgical management?

answers.option: Ultrasound of the bladder and post-void residual volume

question: During the removal of a Foley catheter, the balloon fragments, and a piece of the latex remains within the bladder. Which of the following is the most appropriate method to retrieve this fragment to prevent it from becoming a nidus for stone formation?

answers.option: Perurethral retrieval using a cystoscope and grasping forceps
Vigorous bladder wash with saline through a new Foley catheter

question: A 1-year-old boy is brought for a check-up where the right testis is found to be non-palpable. Which of the following is considered the most accurate "investigation" for both determining the location of an intra-abdominal testis and planning the orchidopexy?

answers.option: CT Scan of the abdomen and pelvis

question: A 4-year-old boy presents with a painless, transilluminating scrotal swelling. The diagnosis of a vaginal hydrocele is made. Which of the following best describes this condition?

answers.option: Collection of blood within the tunica vaginalis following trauma
Fluid localized specifically within the spermatic cord
Fluid collection in the tunica vaginalis due to a patent processus vaginalis communicating with the peritoneum
A swelling in the inguinal region often confused with an indirect hernia
Fluid collection in the tunica vaginalis limited to the scrotum

question: A patient presents with an enlarged spleen and pancytopenia. The clinician notes that the cytopenia is a direct result of increased splenic sequestering and destruction of blood cells, and that the blood counts return to normal following a splenectomy. What is this clinical syndrome known as?

A patient undergoes a splenectomy for trauma. On the 8th postoperative day, the patient develops fever, severe abdominal pain, and an elevated WBC count. A CT scan reveals ascites and mild pneumatosis (gas) in the small intestinal wall. What is the most likely vascular complication?

A 70-year-old male presents with deep bone pain in his lower back. Imaging of the spine reveals multiple osteoblastic (sclerotic) lesions. Which of the following primary malignancies is the most likely source?
Regarding infections in post-organ transplant patients receiving immunosuppressive therapy, which of the following statements is most accurate?

answers.option: Cytomegalovirus represents a major opportunistic threat during the first 6 months
Fungal infections are extremely rare compared to the general population
Protozoal infections like Toxoplasma are unheard of
Bacterial infections are the only concern in the first year
The highest risk of all infections occurs after the first 24 months

question: A patient with a suspected non-functioning kidney due to chronic hydronephrosis requires an assessment to see how much each individual kidney contributes to overall renal function. Which of the following is the best test for this?

A 45-year-old patient with a BMI of 42 kg/m2 has multiple comorbidities, including hypertension, Type 2 Diabetes, and hyperlipidemia. Which procedure is currently favored for providing the most significant metabolic improvement and long-term resolution of these conditions?

A patient has had an asymptomatic umbilical mass for one year. Over the last month, the mass has increased in size and become painful and tender to the touch. The mass is firm and cannot be reduced, but the patient continues to have regular bowel movements and no vomiting. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A female patient presents with a palpable mass in the groin, located lateral to the pubic tubercle and below the inguinal ligament. A cough impulse is positive. Given the high risk of incarceration associated with this specific anatomical location, what is the most appropriate management?

answers.option: Aspiration of the mass under ultrasound guidance
Surgical closure of the femoral canal

question: A patient is suspected of having rectal cancer located 3 mm from the anal verge. Which of the following is the most appropriate method to obtain a tissue sample for histological diagnosis?

answers.option: Digital rectal examination with brush cytology

question: A patient develops a significant right-sided pleural effusion following an esophagectomy. Pleural fluid analysis reveals a milky appearance with a high triglyceride content (>110 mg/dL). What is the most likely cause?

answers.option: Reactive effusion due to postoperative adhesions

question: A patient who underwent a gastric bypass 4 days ago presents with persistent vomiting, abdominal pain, and tachycardia (110 bpm). An X-ray shows dilated loops of small bowel. What is the immediate next step in the management of this suspected early postoperative obstruction?

answers.option: Rapid administration of IV fluid boluses only
Immediate return to the operating theater
Insertion of a nasogastric tube for decompression
Administration of IV opioids and anti-emetics

question: A physically fit patient is diagnosed with a periampullary carcinoma. Staging CT shows no evidence of distant metastasis or major vascular involvement. What is the treatment of choice?

answers.option: Local excision followed by adjuvant radiation

question: A patient is found to have a large (>6 cm) peripancreatic fluid collection (pseudocyst) 6 weeks after an episode of acute pancreatitis. The patient is currently asymptomatic and tolerating a full diet. What is the most appropriate management?

A patient with blunt abdominal trauma presents with a distended abdomen and hypotension. Following the primary survey and initial fluid resuscitation, the patient’s hemodynamics have stabilized and continue to improve. According to ATLS protocols, what is the next best step?

answers.option: Resuscitate with blood products for 2 more hours
Repeat the primary survey to ensure stability

question: A patient is admitted with mild gallstone pancreatitis. The clinical symptoms have resolved, and the serum amylase levels have returned to normal. When should the cholecystectomy be performed to prevent recurrent attacks?

answers.option: Immediately after ERCP in a separate admission
Only if a second attack occurs

question: A patient is on the 6th postoperative day following an esophagectomy with a cervical anastomosis. A small amount of saliva is noted draining from the neck wound, but the patient is otherwise asymptomatic, afebrile, and has no signs of sepsis. What is the next best step?

answers.option: Immediate endoscopy and placement of a covered stent
Urgent surgical revision of the anastomosis
Total parenteral nutrition with "nothing by mouth" for 4 weeks

question: A male patient sustains a pelvic fracture and a confirmed urethral injury. Which of the following is considered the most common long-term complication of this injury?
A patient is diagnosed with low-grade Gastric Mucosa-Associated Lymphoid Tissue (MALT) lymphoma. Biopsies confirm the presence of Helicobacter pylori. What is the first-line treatment?
During a digital rectal examination (DRE) of an elderly man with obstructive voiding symptoms, which finding is most characteristic of benign prostatic hyperplasia?

answers.option: Smooth, firm, elastic enlargement with a mobile rectal mucosa
Loss of the median sulcus with a fixed rectal mucosa

question: For a patient undergoing curative-intent surgery for mid-rectal cancer, which surgical principle is most critical for reducing the rate of local recurrence?

answers.option: Wide local excision of the tumor only

question: A 50-year-old patient is diagnosed with a 3 cm Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST) located on the greater curvature of the gastric body. There is no evidence of local invasion or distant metastasis. What is the surgical treatment of choice?

answers.option: Wedge excision with a 1 cm macroscopic margin

question: During an elective right hemicolectomy for adenocarcinoma of the hepatic flexure, the surgeon discovers a solitary, 2 cm metastatic nodule on the surface of the right lobe of the liver. The patient is stable. What is the most appropriate intraoperative decision?

answers.option: Abandon the procedure and close the patient for systemic chemotherapy
Right hemicolectomy combined with a formal right hepatic lobectomy
Proceed with right hemicolectomy and perform a wedge excision of the liver nodule
Perform the hemicolectomy and refer for postoperative radiation
Complete the hemicolectomy and refer for interval radiofrequency ablation

question: A patient undergoes resection of a high-risk Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST). Molecular markers confirm a c−KIT (CD117) mutation. Which of the following tyrosine kinase inhibitors is the first-line adjuvant agent used to reduce the risk of recurrence?

A 3-year-old boy is brought to the clinic with a reducible right-sided inguinal hernia. Unlike adult hernias, which typically require a mesh repair, what is the standard surgical procedure for a pediatric indirect inguinal hernia?
During an abdominal examination, a clinician palpates a smooth, mobile mass. Which physical sign is most characteristic of a mesenteric cyst, helping to differentiate it from a retroperitoneal mass?

answers.option: The mass is mobile in a plane perpendicular to the attachment of the mesentery
The mass disappears when the patient tenses the abdominal muscles
The mass is fixed and does not move with palpation
The mass moves significantly with respiration

question: What is the most common technical reason for the recurrence of an epigastric hernia following a primary suture repair?

answers.option: Failure to use a large synthetic mesh for a 1 cm defect
Failure to identify and close a second fascial defect during the initial surgery
Excessive physical activity in the first postoperative week

question: A patient presents with a persistent, symptomatic 10×12 cm pancreatic pseudocyst that has failed to resolve after 12 weeks of observation. The cyst wall is well-matured. What is the gold-standard surgical treatment?
A patient presents with sudden-onset, severe "board-like" abdominal rigidity. An erect chest X-ray reveals free air under the diaphragm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

Which imaging modality provides the highest resolution for determining the depth of tumor invasion (T-stage) and the status of the mesorectal fascia in a patient with newly diagnosed rectal adenocarcinoma?
A 55-year-old patient has a rectal cancer that is found to be invading the posterior vaginal wall (T4b) with associated regional lymphadenopathy. What is the current standard of care?

answers.option: Anterior resection followed by adjuvant chemotherapy
Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by surgical resection

question: A patient sustains a penetrating injury to the upper third of the rectum (intraperitoneal portion). There is significant contamination. What is the most appropriate surgical management?

answers.option: Primary closure of the injury with a defunctioning loop colostomy

question: A patient describes a "food-sticking" sensation in the mid-retrosternal area during the involuntary (esophageal) phase of swallowing. What is this specific clinical symptom is defined as?

A patient presents with massive splenomegaly, a platelet count of 40,000/mm3, and a hemoglobin of 8 g/dL. Following splenectomy, both the platelet count and hemoglobin levels normalize. What is this process of inappropriate destruction of healthy blood cells by the spleen is known as?

A 70-year-old male presents with painless, progressive jaundice and a palpable gallbladder (Courvoisier's law). A CT scan reveals a mass compressing the second part of the duodenum. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Carcinoma of the head of the pancreas

question: A 65-year-old patient presents with painless, progressive jaundice and a palpable mass in the right hypochondrium. Imaging confirms a tumor in the head of the pancreas obstructing the common bile duct. According to Courvoisier’s Law, what is the most likely physical finding regarding the gallbladder?

answers.option: Tender, inflamed gallbladder with a positive Murphy’s sign

question: A patient presents with severe epigastric pain of 48 hours' duration. To evaluate the severity of the pancreatitis and predict the risk of pancreatic necrosis or organ failure, which of the following markers is most useful as a standalone acute-phase reactant?

A 28-year-old patient with Crohn's disease is found to have multiple "skip lesions" involving the terminal ileum and cecum. What is the first-line medical therapy used to induce remission in an acute flare?

A 3-year-old child is brought to the clinic after his mother noticed a large, firm, non-tender abdominal mass while bathing him. Imaging reveals a mass arising from the kidney. What is the most common primary renal tumor in this age group?

A patient presents to the emergency department with sudden, severe "loin-to-groin" pain that radiates to the root of the penis and the inner thigh. The patient is unable to find a comfortable position. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 25-year-old male incidentally finds a 2 cm, painless, firm mass in his right testis during a self-examination. What is the gold standard for both definitive diagnosis and initial treatment for a suspected testicular malignancy?

A diabetic patient presents with rapid-onset scrotal swelling, severe pain, and skin crepitus. An ultrasound reveals air within the scrotal tissues (gas gangrene). What is the next best step in management?

A 25-year-old male presents with a gunshot wound to the lower chest. On examination, he is hemodynamically stable, but surgical crepitus is felt over the upper abdomen. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial investigation to screen for pneumothorax or free air under the diaphragm?
A 60-year-old man presents with a 3-month history of weight loss, anemia (Hb:10 g/dL), and a firm, non-tender lump in the right iliac fossa. He is afebrile. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A critically ill burn patient develops right upper quadrant pain. Ultrasound shows gallbladder wall thickening (>4 mm) and pericholecystic fluid, but no stones are visualized. What is the most appropriate management for this patient who is too unstable for general anesthesia?

A patient has completed multimodal treatment for rectal cancer. During follow-up, there is a rising CEA level, but conventional CT imaging is inconclusive. Which scan is most useful for detecting occult distant metastasis or local recurrence?

The incidence of esophageal adenocarcinoma has significantly increased in Western populations over the last few decades. Which of the following is the most significant predisposing factor for this change?
